event_name: Extreme monsoon rainfall over the Krishna basin
affected_region: Sangli, Kolhapur and Satara districts, Maharashtra
historical_description: Mongabay India reported that Sangli, Kolhapur and Satara districts received 1,918 mm of rainfall against a normal average of 333 mm during the late-July to August 2019 spell, seeding the Krishna basin flood situation.

event_name: Panchganga crosses danger mark at Kolhapur
affected_region: Kolhapur city and Panchganga river belt, Maharashtra
historical_description: The Maharashtra Water Resources Department Krishna sub-basin report records that the Panchganga at Rajaram K.T. weir, Kolhapur, exceeded its danger level of 543.30 m on 3 August 2019; the report states the Kolhapur city area remained inundated from 3 to 14 August 2019.

event_name: Krishna crosses danger mark at Irwin Bridge, Sangli
affected_region: Sangli city and Krishna river belt, Maharashtra
historical_description: The Maharashtra Water Resources Department report records that the Krishna at Irwin Bridge, Sangli, exceeded its danger level of 540.77 m on 5 August 2019 and reached a maximum level of 544.57 m on 9 August 2019, receding below danger level from 14 August 2019.

event_name: NH-4 damaged by landslide at Karnataka-Maharashtra border
historical_description: The New Indian Express reported that a vast stretch of NH-4 connecting Pune and Bengaluru was badly damaged by a landslide caused by incessant rain on the Karnataka-Maharashtra border, a key western freight corridor.

event_name: Mass evacuation in Sangli and Kolhapur
historical_description: Wikipedia's chronology of 2019 in India records that over 132,000 people were evacuated in Sangli and Kolhapur districts on 7 August 2019 due to heavy rain and rising rivers.

event_name: Krishna, Warna and Panchganga breach Highest Flood Levels
affected_region: Kurundwad, Arjunwad, Samdoli and Terwad (Kolhapur-Sangli reach)
historical_description: Scroll.in reported that on 8 August 2019 the Krishna breached its Highest Flood Level at Kurundwad and Arjunwad, and that the Warna and Panchganga rivers also crossed their Highest Flood Levels at Samdoli and Terwad.

Wikipedia's article on the 2019 Indian floods states that 70 teams comprising NDRF, Navy, Coast Guard and SDRF personnel were deployed, and that about 400,000 people were evacuated in western Maharashtra.

event_name: NH-4 closed, vehicles stranded during flood peak
historical_description: India Today reported on 10 August 2019 that the NH-4 (Mumbai-Bengaluru national highway) was closed after a landslide, stranding about 18,000 vehicles on the highway.

event_name: Over four lakh moved to safety, water receding
historical_description: The New Indian Express reported that over four lakh people had been moved to safety and that water was receding in Sangli and Kolhapur.

event_name: Aerial survey and displacement survey of affected districts
historical_description: FloodList reported that Union Home Minister Amit Shah carried out an aerial survey of the flood-affected areas of Kolhapur and Sangli on 11 August 2019, and that flooding in Maharashtra had affected 761 villages and displaced over 400,000 people.

event_name: River levels recede below danger marks
affected_region: Kolhapur and Sangli river observation points, Maharashtra
historical_description: The Maharashtra Water Resources Department report records that water levels at Irwin Bridge (Sangli) and Rajaram K.T. weir (Kolhapur) started receding below their danger levels from 14 August 2019.
